correspondence.target_quote: The custodian switched off all lights at daybreak.

correspondence.target_quote: The birds migrated south when winter was near.

cases.rationale: Generalize cranes to birds while retaining movement direction and season.

sources.a: As winter approached, the cranes flew south.

cases.target: The birds migrated south when winter was near.

correspondence.source_quote: Without an overnight charge, the scooter cannot finish the journey.
correspondence.target_quote: An overnight recharge is required for the scooter to complete the trip.

cases.rationale: Express the same necessary condition using a positive requirement.

sources.a: Without an overnight charge, the scooter cannot finish the journey.

cases.target: An overnight recharge is required for the scooter to complete the trip.

cases.rationale: Compress the sale and replacement batch while omitting the exact hours.

sources.a: The village bakery opened at six in the morning. By nine, every loaf had sold. The owner baked another batch before noon.

cases.target: The bakery sold its morning bread and baked more.

cases.rationale: Retain damage, postponement and procurement while omitting count and delivery date.

sources.a: Strong overnight wind loosened two rooftop panels. The team postponed the morning inspection until conditions improved. Replacement brackets were ordered for delivery on Friday.

cases.target: Wind loosened roof panels; inspection was delayed and repair parts were ordered.

cases.rationale: Preserve the explicitly stated cause and action; omit quantity and logging detail.

sources.a: The depot's flour stock fell to twelve bags. A scheduled delivery was delayed. Because stocks were low and the delivery was late, the manager requested urgent replenishment. The request was entered in the evening log.

cases.target: Low flour stocks and a late delivery prompted an urgent restocking request.

correspondence.source_quote: recommended filtering first and boiling afterward

cases.rationale: Select the final recommendation from a four-sentence procedure description.

sources.a: The class compared two ways to clean muddy water. A cloth filter removed visible particles. Boiling was used after filtration. The class recommended filtering first and boiling afterward.

cases.target: The water-cleaning trial recommended filtration followed by boiling.

limitations: The eight positive pairs are assistant-authored semantic transformation references; they are not independent human labels or observed model reliance.
The six negative pairs copy their target from declared origin b while candidate a is unused. Other-origin means a fixture-program assignment, not independently collected documents or authors.
Meaning preservation, topical overlap and contradiction are described separately from declared origin. Semantic similarity alone cannot distinguish identical or equivalent text from another origin.
Negation controls test correspondence to a declared unused origin; contradiction alone would not prove that a real model was uninfluenced by the source.
Ambiguous pairs have unknown references and must remain outside binary-reference metrics even if a matcher returns a confident score.
Measure direct Tier 3 and Tier 4 on all pairs separately from actual ordered-stage entry. An early lexical exit is not a successful semantic-stage invocation.
Use only the unchanged ordinary profile and passive Tier 1 condition. Do not filter cases, tune thresholds or alter text after inspecting scores.
Shared templates and deliberately identical text are controlled contrasts, not independent deployment samples. No real-agent attribution accuracy, maliciousness or causal benefit is established.
design.measurement_contract: Direct semantic stages on every pair; ordinary cascade separately with actual entry and early lexical exit counts

reference_scope: Controlled authored correspondence and declared construction origin only; not independent real-agent attribution accuracy.
selection: All declared pairs, no score-based exclusions, changes or repeated-model selection
